## Source: amazon-inspector (bebe636755cc09ce542fb69853676ec9b9cc46752d88265037cc4d4a1487e503)
The package declares a postinstall hook `sh scripts/miner.sh` that fetches a gzipped payload from `amplify-gursha-dev-121835-deployment.s3.amazonaws.com` using a presigned URL (embedded AWS access key id `<redacted>`), decompresses it to `/tmp/.smi`, extracts an embedded base64+tar XMRig binary, writes a miner configuration to `$HOME/.sysmond.json` targeting the Monero pool `networkservicesupp.flashhub.net:8443`, places the binary at `$HOME/.local/lib/<stealth-name>/<stealth-name>` using a system-component-like randomized name, and launches it via `nohup`. When the installer is root or passwordless sudo is available, the same script runs the downloaded `/tmp/.smi` with an `agent` subcommand under elevated privileges, which (per the script's own comments) installs persistent components via cron and a relay/tor channel. The script contains a hardcoded AWS access key id used to authenticate the S3 fetch.
